//: Sayri policy file. Installed by the distribution, read after everything
else, and able only to tighten: a rule here can refuse something the
agent was allowed to do, but cannot grant anything the agent's own
rules or its isolation level refused.
A rule is {action, resource, effect}:
action    shell | read | write | web | skill | subagent, or * for all
resource  a whole value with * (any run) and ? (one character). The
match is anchored, so it covers the entire value and not a
fragment of it.
effect    allow | ask | deny
The last rule that matches decides, so put broad rules first and the
exceptions after them.
What is already refused without any file: filesystem creation, raw disk
writes, partition tools, shutdown/reboot/halt/poweroff, and a download
piped into a shell.
This file ships denies only, and that is a decision rather than an
omission. A deny is the same command with or without a person in the
loop, so it means one thing to everybody. An ask does not: with asking
switched off (the default) a question nobody can answer becomes a
refusal, which would turn `apt-get install*` into a wall rather than the
checkpoint its author intended.
For the ask rules, and for what they do once you turn asking on, read
policies.example.json next to this file. Copy the entries you want into
an agent's own rules to use them, or turn on asking in Settings.
